COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Network Security, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Security.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Security.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Network Security.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.

2. When learning Logic Gates, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Gates.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Gates.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Gates.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Logic Gates.

3. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Remove all guards

4. When learning Binary Arithmetic Operations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

5. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Information and Communication Technology
   C. Internal Cooking Timer
   D. Input Cable Tester

6. When learning Object Oriented Programming Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

7. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Monitor
   B. Speaker
   C. Keyboard
   D. CPU

8. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.

9. When learning Relational Database Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Relational Database Fundamentals.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.

10. When learning Object Oriented Programming Implementation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

11. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.

12. When learning Computer Network Standards and Protocols, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Network Standards and Protocols.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Gates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Circuits and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Network Standards and Protocols and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Network Security and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
